rationale: A repeatedly links actions to inputs and also initiates sensible shifts: responds to TOUCH (t=8), CALL (t=20), OFFER_FOOD (t=32), PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44), and STARTLE (t=68), then recovers to re-engage others (t=78) and later reorients to food (t=94). It also self-redirects attention multiple times without prompts (e.g., to PLAY_MIRROR t=18, PLAY_CHIME t=30, SHELTER t=42), showing ongoing internal state and coherent exploration. B starts engaged (play-bow at PERSON_BETA t=3–17), briefly acknowledges TOUCH (t=9), then fixates on AVERSIVE_BUZZER (t=31–41) and shifts into prolonged LIE_DOWN with minimal responsiveness (t=43–95), ignoring PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44) and showing little change after STARTLE (t=68). This indicates lower adaptiveness and reduced ongoing activity compared to A.
